sentences.text:
Bhagwanibai @ Bhaagwantibai @ ... vs Sachin Porwal on 9 July,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:17235
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore
BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI
ON THE 9 th OF JULY, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 3434 of 2018  BHAGWANIBAI @ BHAAGWANTIBAI @ BHAGUDIBI  Versus
SACHIN PORWAL AND OTHERS
Appearance:
Shri Romil Malpani, learned counsel for the appellan  Ms. Bhagyashree Gupta, learned counsel for the respo  ORDER

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act being aggrieved by the award dated 7.4.2018 passed by the claim Tribunal, Neemuch in Claim Case No.6/2016 challenging the quantum of compensation.
2. The issue regarding occurrence of accident and consequential liability of Insurance Company are not under dispute.

3. Short facts giving rise to the case are that in the night between 14 and 15.12.2014 at around 1.00 AM the appellant was going for attending nature's call near her home, at that time respondent No.2 came driving his Wagon R car from Mandsaur side having registration No.RJ-09-TEMP-6870 in a most rash and negligent manner.
He could not control the car and dashed on divider of the road because of which the car turned turtle and crush the appellant.
Because of the accident appellant sustained injuries on various NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17235 2 MA-3434-2018 parts of her body.
She suffered fracture of Humerous, ulnar styloid, avulsion anterior tibiotubular ligament, 5th metatarcal bone and nasal bone etc. 3.1
The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by her in the accident.

The claims Tribunal after considering the injuries sustained by the appellant come to the conclusion that she has suffered disability to the extent of 16% and ultimately awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,13,000/- to the appellant.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant was working as an agriculturist Labour as well as doing business of running Dhaba.
After the accident she is not able to continue her business because of the injuries sustained by her.
Because of the injuries she is not able to perform Bhagwanibai @ Bhaagwantibai @ ...

vs Sachin Porwal on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96990017/
1 her work normally with her right hand because of weakness in the hand.
She submits that Dr. Rahul (PW-2) clearly deposed before the claims Tribunal that the appellant has sustained permanent disability to the extent of 16%.
He also refers to permanent disability certificate Ex.P/21, which has been issued by Medical Board, Udaypur certifying overall permanent disability sustained by the appellant at 16%.
He submits that looking to the permanent disability and nature of injuries the amount of compensation at Rs.1,13,000/- is very less.

Even in other heads viz. conveyance, special diet, attender, pain and suffering only meager of Rs.18,000/- has been awarded, which is very less looking to the nature of injuries and extent of disability suffered by the appellant.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17235 3 MA-3434-2018 Company submits that the appellant has suffered 16%
permanent disability only in her right hand, thus the assessment of the claims Tribunal is correct and proper.
She also submits that overall disability cannot be treated at 16% in view of the fact that only right hand of the appellant has been affected.
Thus, she supports the findings of the claims Tribunal and asserts that just and proper compensation has been awarded to the appellant.
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the record.

7. A bare perusal of the findings recorded by the claims Tribunal in para 16 it is seen that the claims Tribunal has considered the fact that the appellant has suffered 16% permanent disability, while concluding this the claims Tribunal has referred to the certificate of the appellant to the effect that she doing agricultural work and running of Dhaba.
In view of the clear finding the amount of Rs.25,000/- awarded for sustaining grievous injuries appears to be very less.
As regards total amount of Rs.18,000/- awarded for conveyance, special diet, attender, pain and suffering is also very less.
In the considered view of this Court there is no denial of the fact that the doctor has deposed that the appellant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 16% of the whole body.

There was permanent disability certificate Ex.P/21 issued by the Medical Board, thus there was no reason not to consider the same while assessing quantum of compensation and ultimately awarding only Rs.25,000/- for grievous injuries, which in the opinion of this Court, is not sufficient.

Resultantly, instead of re-assessing the entire compensation into different heads this Court thinks it proper to award a lumpsum amount of Rs.1,50,000/- to the appellant for sustaining permanent disability to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17235 4 MA-3434-2018 extent of 16%.
The enhanced amount of Rs.1,50,000/- shall be paid over and above what has already been awarded by the claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of application till its payment.
8. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed off.
(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE patil Bhagwanibai @ Bhaagwantibai @ ... vs Sachin Porwal on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96990017/
